title: Derived adjunction between extension and restriction of scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category (closed means that
 each fixed-factor tensor functor has a right adjoint) whose tensor product is additive in each variable, and which has a functorial flat resolution, meaning a functor $P\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$
with flat values and a natural epimorphism $P(M)\twoheadrightarrow M$ (flat means that tensoring on either
side is exact). Let $\varphi\colon\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects
(commutative monoid objects) of $\mathcal C$. For $T=\mathcal R,\mathcal S$, let $\Mod_T(\mathcal C)$ be
the category of $T$-module objects (objects with unital associative $T$-actions). For an $\mathcal R$-module $M$, define extension of scalars by the relative tensor product
$$
\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(M)=\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M
=\operatorname{coeq}\Bigl((\mu_{\mathcal S}\circ(1_{\mathcal S}\otimes\varphi))\otimes1_M,
(1_{\mathcal S}\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha\Bigr),
$$
where $\gamma_M$ is the $\mathcal R$-action and $\alpha$ is the canonical associator; let $\mathcal S$
act on the first factor. For an $\mathcal S$-module $N$, define restriction of scalars by leaving the
underlying object and morphism unchanged and giving it the $\mathcal R$-action
$\mathcal R\otimes N\xrightarrow{\varphi\otimes N}\mathcal S\otimes N\xrightarrow{\gamma_N}N$. These functors have the
canonical adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. For an abelian
category $\mathcal A$, write $D(\mathcal A)$ for the unbounded localization of cochain complexes at
quasi-isomorphisms; a complex of $T$-modules is K-flat if it is K-flat for the relative tensor product $\otimes_T$ of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] in the sense of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], i.e. tensoring with it on either side sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms,
and a K-injective complex is one receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes. The symbols $L$
and $R$ denote total left and right derived functors computed on K-flat and K-injective resolutions,
respectively, whenever the corresponding resolutions and preservation hypotheses hold. Then the adjunction derives to
$$
L(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi)\dashv R(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)
$$
between $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C))$ and $D(\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C))$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A_T=\Mod_T(\mathcal C)$ for $T=\mathcal R,\mathcal S$, with exactly the ambient hypotheses of [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-kflat]. For each of these commutative ring objects, [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] makes $\mathcal A_T$ Grothendieck abelian. By [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] its relative tensor is closed symmetric monoidal: $M\otimes_T-$ has right adjoint $\Hom_T(M,-)$. By [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions], the assumed functorial flat resolution of $\mathcal C$ supplies a functorial flat resolution in $\mathcal A_T$. All three statements assume a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian ambient category with additive tensor and a commutative ring object; those are precisely the present hypotheses. The last statement additionally assumes the ambient functorial flat resolution, which is also given.

source.place: second sentence: structural hypotheses, expanded using sk-prop-sfb-module-category, proof Part 3

proof.text: Verify the remaining source hypotheses of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. By [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], each $\mathcal A_T$ has small colimits and exact filtered colimits. Thus it has countable coproducts and exact ordered-$\mathbf Z$ colimits: any finite set of integers has an upper bound, so this index category is filtered. For any adjunction $H\dashv J$ and small diagram $D$, the natural bijections $\Hom(H(\operatorname{colim}D),Y)\cong\Hom(\operatorname{colim}D,JY)\cong\lim_i\Hom(D_i,JY)\cong\lim_i\Hom(HD_i,Y)$ show directly that $H$ preserves this colimit. Apply this to the fixed-factor tensor functors in $\mathcal C$, using its assumed closedness and symmetry, and in $\mathcal A_T$, using [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom]. In particular these functors preserve countable coproducts and ordered-$\mathbf Z$ colimits. They also preserve zero and finite coproducts, hence finite biproducts. They are additive: the biproduct injection/projection equations determine the diagonal $\Delta$, codiagonal $\nabla$, and $a\oplus b$, and under the canonical biproduct identifications their images are those same maps. Applying the functor to $a+b=\nabla(a\oplus b)\Delta$ therefore gives $H(a+b)=H(a)+H(b)$; the zero map factors through the preserved zero object. This verifies tensor additivity in both variables without assuming that arbitrary tensor functors are exact.

source.place: second sentence: full left-derived source hypotheses

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ and $U=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. Clause 2 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] supplies $E\dashv U$: the ambient category is symmetric, has coequalizers since it is abelian, and tensoring preserves colimits by step 2; $\mathcal R$ is commutative. This left adjoint $E$ preserves zero and binary coproducts by the explicit adjoint-colimit argument in step 2. The biproduct formula from that step therefore gives $E(a+b)=E(a)+E(b)$ and $E(0)=0$. Restriction is the identity on underlying objects and morphisms by clause 1 of the cited statement, so it preserves the sums and zero of module morphisms and is additive as well. Thus this is an adjunction of additive functors between the abelian module categories of step 1.

source.place: last sentence: the underived additive adjunction

proof.text: For every quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to P'$ between K-flat $\mathcal R$-module complexes, [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-kflat] gives that $E(s)=\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}s$ is a quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal S$-modules. Consequently the left-derived clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] applies to $E$, by steps 1–3, giving $LE$ on the unbounded derived category computed on K-flat resolutions. The category $\mathcal A_{\mathcal S}$ is Grothendieck by step 1, so [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] supplies K-injective resolutions of all its unbounded complexes. The right-derived clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] therefore supplies $RU$, computed by applying $U$ to those resolutions. The resolution category for this right derived functor is $\mathcal S$-modules, not $\mathcal R$-modules. No claim that $U$ preserves K-injectives is needed.

source.place: first two sentences: preservation of K-flat quasi-isomorphisms and K-injective resolutions

proof.text: Apply the derived-adjunction clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] with $f=E:\mathcal A_{\mathcal R}\to\mathcal A_{\mathcal S}$ and $g=U$ and the ordinary adjunction from step 3. Its hypotheses on the monoidal source, functorial flat resolution and colimits are steps 1–2; additivity is step 3; preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes and target K-injective resolutions are step 4. It provides the natural Hom bijections $a_{K,N}:\Hom_{D(\mathcal A_{\mathcal S})}(LE(K),N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{D(\mathcal A_{\mathcal R})}(K,RU(N))$. Define the indicated derived adjunction to be this adjunction for the functors $LE$ and $RU$. Explicitly its unit is $a_{K,LE(K)}(1_{LE(K)})$ and its counit is $a_{RU(N),N}^{-1}(1_{RU(N)})$; naturality and the inverse identities of these bijections give the triangle identities. This defines exactly $L(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi)\dashv R(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)$, before any identification of the right adjoint with termwise restriction.

source.place: last sentence: apply the general derived adjunction
